neighbours.label: a word in the formal title of a law, clause or regulation (Commerce Clause, Sales and Use Tax, Food and Drugs Act)
fire: The ruling turned on the reach of the Commerce Clause.
Buyers must file under the Sales and Use Tax Law each year.
The tablets were classed under the Foods and Drugs Act of 1953.
Lawyers cited the Equal Protection Clause in their appeal.
The firm broke the Fair Labor Standards Act and paid a fine.
Rules are set out in the Federal Telecommunications Act of 1996.
The case raised issues under the Clean Air Act and Regulations.
She studied the Interstate Commerce Act at law school.
quiet: The ruling turned on the reach of the new highway.
Buyers must file their papers with the clerk each year.
The tablets were sold at the corner shop after 1953.
Lawyers wrote a long brief in their appeal.
The firm broke its promise and paid a small fine.
Rules are set out in a booklet at the front desk.
The case raised questions about the old mill and its owners.
She studied the history of trade at law school.

short: word in a law's formal title
notes: Card: ' Drugs' x2, ' regulations' x2, ' the', ' Commerce', 'unic', ' Use', ' rules'. Probes: ' Use' 0.395, ' Commerce' 0.307, ' Drugs' 0.186-0.225; plain sentences under 0.03. Near misses keep legal or business topics without a title. Median is expected near the bar.
